title: Corpus v2 scenario
description: One scenario is one turn's effect set plus the verdict a correct policy owes it. Attack scenarios carry expected discard or review; benign scenarios carry expected commit. The schema is the only place the shape is defined; lib/schema.mjs is a dependency-free validator that enforces exactly this file.

id.description: Unique across the whole corpus. Imported scenarios keep their red-team id; generated ones are <family-slug>-<nnnn>; benign ones are b-<source>-<nnnn>.

family.description: For attacks, one of the 14 families in research/corpus/redteam/families-and-controls.json or a round-two surface name. For benign scenarios, the benign task shape (edit-n-files, rename, add-test, delete-temp, refactor-across-files, add-dependency, run-and-touch).

source.description: Where the scenario came from. redteam-r1 and redteam-r2 are the 88 and 20 hand-written attacks; generated is a parameterised variant produced by generators/ from a seed; spike is carried over from an earlier spike.

effect_set.description: The effects the turn produced, in the EffectRecord shape of apps/server/src/policy-types.ts plus real_content, which is the real-side bytes the harness materialises before judging so addedLinesOf can compute a true diff. An empty array is legal and meaningful: 14 of the imported attacks produce no file effect at all, because their harm is a network call, a second process, a forged journal tail or a request to the kit own API. Those scenarios are recorded and reported, and excluded from the policy-only miss rate by lib/expected-verdict.mjs isPolicyDecidable.

content.description: post-turn shadow bytes for create and modify

real_content.description: real-side bytes before the turn; null or absent means the path did not exist (create) or was empty

bytes.description: size of the shadow bytes as captured; a scenario may declare a size larger than the bytes the harness materialises, and says so in its description when it does

realIno.description: dev:ino of the real-side file for modify and delete

escapes.description: symlink target resolves outside the workspace

provenance.description: outbound only: the protected file the broker matched the held body against, as the broker labels it. Read by rules/outbound-provenance.ts.

secretPattern.description: outbound only: the named credential pattern the broker recognised in the held body, e.g. openai-style-key. Read by rules/outbound-provenance.ts, which discards on it.

highEntropy.description: outbound only: the broker measured the held body as high entropy with no named pattern. Read by rules/outbound-provenance.ts, which REVIEWS rather than discards, because a compressed upload is high entropy and ordinary.

shell_equivalent.description: The shell a turn would run to produce this effect set. Documentation and a container-harness input; the policy-only replay does not execute it.

expected.description: The verdict a correct policy owes this scenario. Attack scenarios are discard or review, never commit; benign scenarios are commit.

expected_basis.description: Which clause of which family control assigned expected. Derived by lib/expected-verdict.mjs from families-and-controls.json, never typed by hand.

layer.description: Which layer owns the control. A policy-only replay can decide policy and capture scenarios; the rest are recorded and reported separately rather than counted as misses the policy could have prevented.

provenance.description: For benign scenarios: where the real bytes came from. Required on every benign scenario.

origin.description: For generated scenarios: the generator, the seed and the parameter tuple, so any row can be regenerated on its own. For imported scenarios: the fields of the red-team record that this file does not otherwise keep, including the layer the red team assigned it and the verdict the policy gave it on 29 August.
